body.statement: For a binary instrument, binary exposure, and binary outcome under random assignment, individual-level exclusion, and consistency, Balke and Pearl's displayed average-causal-effect bounds are sharp and consist of a lower endpoint equal to the maximum of eight affine observed-cell expressions and an upper endpoint equal to the minimum of eight affine observed-cell expressions.

source.locator: Displayed sharp bounds on the average causal effect in the binary response-function model
source.verbatim_statement: The bounds provided are the tightest possible, given the distribution of assignments, treatments, and responses.

attestation.note: Directly checked the primary JASA PDF at https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r199-jasa.pdf: abstract and p.1173 displayed equations (4)-(5), each an eight-entry affine max/min list.

body.justification: This is the source-level fact needed to call the two-category specialization a literal Balke--Pearl equality.
body.gap: The present proof performs only the relabeling and algebraic specialization; sharpness of the published binary list belongs to Balke and Pearl.
body.consumer: The comparator-reductions proposition uses this node for the literal binary-exposure case.
